name: Dogme 95
summary: A film made under a written vow: handheld camera, real locations, available light and the sound of the scene. The rules remove the tools that fake the world, so the actors and the room carry the film.

philosophy.core_thesis: A fixed set of prohibitions removes illusion, polish and the director's taste, so that the truth of the scene remains.
design_principles: Shoot on location with the props that are already there; bring in no set piece.
Hold the camera in the hand for every shot; keep the camera at 1.4 to 1.7 m and let it search, with reframes every 3 to 8 s.
Light only with the available light; if the room is too dark, fix one lamp to the camera and nothing else.
Shoot in colour at 4:3 or Academy 1.37:1, at 25 fps (PAL) or 24 fps, with a 180° shutter and no filter.
Record sound with the picture; add no music unless it plays in the room where the scene is shot.
Cut at an average shot length of 4 to 8 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title) with jump cuts that stay in the film.
Use no genre and no superficial action: no murder, no weapon; keep the time and place of the story in the here and now.
Leave the director out of the credits.
anti_patterns: A tripod, a dolly or a crane
Added music or sound effects laid under a scene
Studio lighting, a lit set or a coloured filter
Optical effects and a post-produced colour grade
A genre film with set-piece action
A director credit and a signature style

composition.framing: A loose 4:3 frame; a head can touch the edge and a back can block the view for 1 to 3 s.
composition.staging_in_depth: The camera moves through the room among 3 to 8 people; the foreground is often an obstruction.
composition.subject_placement: Wherever the actor stands; the frame follows, late by 0.2 to 0.5 s, and then corrects.

principles.rule: Shoot a 4:3 frame by hand and let the head or the back cut the frame for 1 to 3 s.
principles.value: head or back cuts 10% to 25% of the frame for 1 to 3 s

principles.rule: Let the frame follow the actor late by 0.2 to 0.5 s and then correct, so the subject is never fixed.
Put the camera in the room among the people, with the foreground as an obstruction.
Use only the light in the room: no added lamp, no filter.
Hold one handheld, un-graded look for the whole film, with no optical effect.

camera_and_movement.movement: Handheld at all times, with a visible search for the action: a late pan, a jerk, a reframe. No stabiliser.
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Walking pace, 1.0 to 1.5 m/s; reframe pans of 30° to 90° in under 1 s

lens_and_format.focal_length: Zoom on a small camcorder, about 35mm to 60mm (35mm format) at the wide-to-mid end
lens_and_format.focus: Autofocus that hunts; focus loss is part of the film.

light.quality: Available light only: window, lamp and street. Faces drop into shadow and highlights clip.
light.direction: Wherever the room puts it; the actor can be against the window.
light.colour_temperature: Mixed 3200K tungsten and 5600K daylight, left uncorrected
light.source: Room lights, windows, one lamp fixed to the camera

colour_and_grade.treatment: Un-graded colour. Mixed white balance and the limits of the DV sensor are the look.
grade_recipe: Keep the camera white balance; set no LUT.
Correct only exposure: set the black point at 5% and the white point at 100%.
Leave the mixed colour temperature: 3200K and 5600K in one frame.
Keep the noise and the compression; add no grain.
Add no vignette and no sharpening beyond the camera default.
colour_and_grade.texture: DV compression blocks and sensor noise, amount 8% to 12%

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 4 to 8 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 1 s to 90 s for a long scene take
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut on the performance. Cover a scene with 1 to 3 takes and keep the lost focus and the shake.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut and jump cut only; no dissolve, no fade, no effect.

sound.approach: Sound and picture are recorded together; no sound is made apart from the image.
sound.dialogue: Overlapping, natural, with room tone; no post-dubbing.
sound.music: Only music that plays in the room, such as a radio or a band at a party.
sound.loudness: −23 LUFS integrated (EBU R128), no limiter pumping

titles_and_graphics.treatment: A plain card with the title and the Dogme certificate number; no director credit.
titles_and_graphics.type: White sans-serif on black, 1 to 3 s, no animation.

shot_primer.opening: Open inside the room with the camera already moving; no establishing shot and no music.

positive: real location with no set dressing

emotion.target_response: Discomfort and honesty: the viewer is in the room and cannot look away.

use_cases: video prompts for a raw family scene
avoid_when: The brief needs a polished product or a hero shot.
The piece must look good at a glance on a phone feed.

modifiers.how: Keep the handheld camera and the location; move to 35mm black and white at 24 fps, add a bounce light and allow a music cue.
Keep the handheld camera and the room tone; address the lens, shoot 16:9 and allow cuts to remove every pause.

colour_temperature.note: Tungsten and daylight stay mixed and uncorrected.

sources.title: Dogme 95 manifesto and Vow of Chastity (Lars von Trier and Thomas Vinterberg, 1995)
